a.summary: LOST BY v1_tx, ALREADY REAPPLIED IN THIS WORKING TREE — re-verify before committing. main 0d68f02 changed the versioned-branch read from a compact-u16 decode to a raw u8: `invokedIndexes[i] = data[o++] & 0xFF;` (main stage 2, line 69). v1_tx stage 3 line 63 still has `invokedIndexes[i] = decode(data, o); o += getByteLen(data, o);`. Solana serializes program_id_index as a single u8; the compact-u16 form advances the cursor by two bytes whenever the index has the high bit set, desynchronising the whole instruction walk. Merged tree line 77 currently carries main's form.

b.summary: LOST BY v1_tx, ALREADY REAPPLIED IN THIS WORKING TREE — re-verify before committing. main b548021 widened the three u8 message-header counts, with the rationale kept as a comment: "read as signed bytes, a value past 0x7F is a negative count that inflates the signer loops ... instead of being rejected as malformed". main has `numRequiredSignatures = data[o++] & 0xFF;`, `final int numReadonlySignedAccounts = data[o++] & 0xFF;`, `final int numReadonlyUnsignedAccounts = data[o++] & 0xFF;`. v1_tx stage 3 lines 39/45/46 still read `data[o++]` signed on all three. Merged tree lines 50-60 currently carry main's form including the comment.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
